issues.description: Indentation bug: the `if sys.version_info` block sits at module level but the original `class Math_unary` block lost its trailing blank line and the conditional is now glued to the class definition with wrong indentation context.
issues.detail: Look at the diff in `numba/core/typing/mathdecl.py`. The `]` closes the `_signatures` list inside `class Math_unary`, then the blank line is removed and `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` is appended. That conditional registers `infer_global(math.exp2)` against the existing `Math_unary` class, which is fine in principle, but the diff context shows the blank separator between the class body and the next decorator (`@infer_global(math.atan2)`) is being eaten. Read your own diff. The result is harder to read than it has to be, and the style does not match the surrounding file where each `@infer_global` block is cleanly separated. Fix the whitespace and put the version-guarded registration *after* a clean blank line, not jammed against the class.

issues.description: `sys` is imported in `mathdecl.py` but the two `mathimpl.py` files use `sys.version_info` without importing `sys`. This will NameError at import time on Python 3.11+.
issues.detail: The diff adds `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` to `numba/cpython/mathimpl.py` and `numba/np/math/mathimpl.py`, but the diff does not show an `import sys` being added to either file. If `sys` happens to already be imported there, fine — but the patch author needs to show that, not hope. As submitted, this is the kind of patch that compiles in the author's head and breaks at `import numba` on a fresh interpreter. Does it run? Did you actually try `python -c 'import numba'` on 3.11? Show me.

issues.description: The version guard is the wrong shape. `math.exp2` exists in CPython since 3.11; numba should either support it on the Python versions it claims to support, or not. Three separate `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` sprinkles is special-casing.
issues.detail: This is a taste issue. You have the same conditional in three files plus a fourth in the test. If numba already requires Python >= 3.11 (check `setup.py` / `pyproject.toml`), all four guards are dead code — delete them. If numba still supports 3.10, then the guards are correct but should route through one central capability check (e.g., `numba.core.utils.PYVERSION` which the test already uses) rather than `sys.version_info` in some files and `PYVERSION` in others. Pick one. Right now the patch uses two different mechanisms for the same check, which is BAD-TASTE.

issues.description: Missing newline at end of `docs/upcoming_changes/10276.new_feature.rst` — the diff explicitly shows `\ No newline at end of file`.
issues.detail: Trivial, but the diff literally announces it. Add the trailing newline. This is the kind of thing a pre-commit hook should catch; if numba has one, run it.

issues.description: Test `x_values` for `test_exp2` is a copy-paste of `test_exp` and does not include any value that would distinguish `exp2` from `exp` semantically.
issues.detail: `exp2(x) == 2**x`. A useful test would include integer values where `2**x` is exact and the result is obvious (e.g., `exp2(0) == 1`, `exp2(1) == 2`, `exp2(10) == 1024`). Right now the test only verifies that the numba implementation matches the Python one for the same arbitrary inputs used for `exp` — that catches a wrong-intrinsic regression by coincidence, not by intent. Not a blocker, but the next maintainer would write better test values.

issues.description: Commit/RST blurb is content-free: "Support for math.exp2 is added."
issues.detail: The release note says what the title already says. Tell the reader *why* it matters or at least what versions it applies to ("Available on Python 3.11+, where `math.exp2` exists in the standard library"). Release notes are for the user, not the patch tracker.

review.summary: Small, well-scoped feature patch that mostly follows the existing pattern for unary math intrinsics — that part is GOOD-TASTE, it slots into `unary_math_intr` the same way `exp`/`log2` do. But the patch was not actually run before submission: two of the three files use `sys.version_info` without an `import sys` visible in the diff, the indentation around the new `if` block in `mathdecl.py` is sloppy and breaks the file's voice, and the same version check is done two different ways (`sys.version_info` vs `PYVERSION`) which is the kind of inconsistency a maintainer six months from now will curse. The release note has a trailing-newline violation and says nothing useful. NEEDS-WORK: fix the imports, unify the version check on `PYVERSION`, clean the whitespace, add a trailing newline, and add at least one test value that exercises `2**x` semantics. Then it lands.
